<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822__p007">
  <section v="18">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that there are two types of miracles: a change in the form and nature of creations, and a change in their very material existence, each enabled by the corresponding nullification of the creation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is that in miracles there are two types,</t>
    <t s="1">a change in the form and nature of creations</t>
    <t s="2">(like the splitting of the Sea of Reeds where the waters stood like a wall)</t>
    <t s="3">and a change in the very existence of their material substance</t>
    <t s="4">(like the miracle that the water turned to blood and that the staff turned into a serpent),</t>
    <t s="5">for through the nullification that is in the form of creations</t>
    <t s="6">(for the coming into being of form is from the Will)</t>
    <t s="7">they are like vessels for the miracle of change of form and nature,</t>
    <t s="8">and through the nullification that is in their very existence</t>
    <t s="9">(for the coming into being of their existence has no place in intellect)</t>
    <t s="10">they are like vessels for the miracle of change of their very existence.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="19">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that conversely, for the supernal to be drawn into the natural world, there must be a parallel of nature within the supernal, which is why the blessing mentions multiple types of miracles.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that correspondingly it is on the other side,</t>
    <t s="3">that in order for that which is above nature to be drawn into the nature of the world,</t>
    <t s="4">it is through that which is above nature having a likeness of nature.</t>
    <t s="5">And this is "Blessed is He Who performed miracles" in the plural,</t>
    <t s="6">a multiplicity of types of miracles,</t>
    <t s="7">for it may be said that from the reasons that there are a multiplicity of miracles,</t>
    <t s="8">even though the matter of multiplicity</t>
    <t s="9">(division)</t>
    <t s="10">is in the chain of descent and the root which is above nature is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="11">it is in order that through this it will be possible for the drawing down of that which is above nature into the nature of the world.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="20">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the two general categories of miracles as taught by the Rebbe Rashab: miracles above nature and miracles clothed in natural ways, with further subdivisions regarding how the natural garment reveals or conceals the miracle.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the matter of the multiplicity of types in miracles is explained by the Rebbe</t>
    <t s="1">(Moharashab)</t>
    <t s="2">of blessed memory in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="3">that in general they are divided into two types33.</t>
    <t s="4">Miracles that are above nature,</t>
    <t s="5">and miracles that are clothed in natural ways.</t>
    <t s="6">And in particular,</t>
    <t s="7">even within the miracles that are clothed in nature itself there are two types.</t>
    <t s="8">The garments of nature are in a manner that it is recognizable in them that they are only a garment for the miracle that is clothed in them,</t>
    <t s="9">like the miracles of Chanukah and Purim</t>
    <t s="10">(and likewise the miracles of the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev and Yud Beis Tammuz)</t>
    <t s="11">that despite their being clothed in natural ways,</t>
    <t s="12">nevertheless the miracle within them was revealed and apparent</t>
    <t s="13">(to the extent that all the ends of the earth saw)</t>
    <t s="14">the miracle within them.</t>
    <t s="15">And the garments of nature conceal and hide the miracle that is clothed in them.</t>
    <t s="16">To the extent that sometimes they conceal and hide it completely,</t>
    <t s="17">so that it is not at all recognizable that it is a miracle,</t>
    <t s="18">"the master of the miracle does not recognize his miracle"34.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
